<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 72 pages)`

The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **18** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 688052e147f23a15e127070ff1bc7c1572de09ab` → `packageMentionDocs`.

## 席位核对

Seat review · `domain:engine` seat 2 · `session_01QK6pdbxKZiHdFApL8RYVh9` · 2026-10-21T07:21Z · head `549f0bcc8` · verdict: **ACCEPT** (`TIER_DEFAULT`, this lane seat's own review). The PR touches none of the four contract faces: no `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed text, `Clause-②: no`, and no `yes` declaration.

- **Shape.** A draft PR to `main` from the claimed branch `claude/issue-25010-readable-ids-nested-compose`. The body's only card keyword is `Fixes #25010`.
  - The branch was built on PR #25032's branch, as the claim directed (6307546021).
  - After PR #25032 landed (`f8c5fb396`), the branch merged `origin/main` in one true merge, `70d95b3e2`.
  - `git diff origin/main...549f0bcc8` is this card's five files alone.
- **Diff, read by the seat** (`engine.ts`, `filter-comparand-shape.ts`):
  - `composeReadableIdsAtBoundary` now resolves the security service once per read and hands the sites to `composeReadableIdsChain`.
  - That method composes every leaf an answered scope carries, before the leaf that encloses it, with the read's context as it stands at every level.
  - D5's two classes are refused at each level before the service is asked: `refuseUncomposableReadableIdsClasses` runs on the nested sites against the read's own object and datasource.
  - A parent's answer is stored only after its nested composition returns, so a chain that reaches back to an ancestor meets the `ancestors` check and is refused as a cycle.
  - The closed doors are unchanged: `null` gives `[]`, and `scope: undefined` composes with no restriction, as before.
  - A scope with no leaf is composed by reference, one level asked, which is the control pin.
  - `collectComposableReadableIds`'s new `at` label only renames the sites' path.
- **Gates on this head.**
  - 41 check-runs: 34 `success`, 7 `skipped`. All 7 skips are in main's roster (`check-expected-skips.mjs --pr 25072`: OK).
  - `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 25072`: NOT governed, +1079/−13.
  - The three families the dev could not run locally are green in CI on this head: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n` run inside the green `Build Core` and lint legs, and `check:type-check-debt` inside the green `Type Check · debt ledger`.
- **Pins.** The refusal cases assert `code` and `status` through one matcher (`{ code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', status: 500 }`): D5.2 and D5.3 at the nested level, a non-`$in` or forged leaf inside a scope, a cycle, and depth past the bound.
  - The real-stack file reads row-for-row parity with today's id-list path, for two direct identities and a delegated caller, and measures one statement.
  - The ablation of the recursion turns those pins red, with the restore proven.
- **Changeset, checked sentence by sentence.**
  - `minor` for `@objectstack/objectql` and `Clause-②: no` match the diff.
  - "the same cut as the `controlled_by_parent` derivation's" holds: `CBP_MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH = 8` (`security-plugin.ts:544`).
  - "every shipped read is served as before" holds, because no shipped service answers a scope that carries a leaf until card (c).
- **Accepted deviations.**
  - The stacked base, as claimed.
  - The real-stack parity pin emulates the plugin-security switch on the test side, as declared.
  - The probe test was written and deleted before any commit.
  - Four `as any` casts were fixed in `549f0bcc8`, with the ratchet held at 236.
- **Seat note, no carrier.** The depth bound is checked when a parent is first answered, and an answer is reused by reference wherever that parent appears again. So in a diamond-shaped master graph, a parent first composed near the top and reused deep inside another branch can nest more than 8 subqueries without a refusal.
  - The bound is a cost ceiling, not a security line (the docblock says so), and the closed doors hold at every level.
  - Every authored chain is one hop, and the deepest anyone has asked for is two.
  - Recorded, not reworked.
- **Out of scope.**
  - The Turso remote transport's refusal of a nested composed leaf has no reach until card (c). It is recorded on #24932 as that switch's prerequisite (6309967905).
  - ADR-0139 D2 step 2's "the same lowering" sentence against `readableIdsScopeOf`, which hands the scope through as answered: governed text, source reading, no carrier.
  - The id-list pre-scan stays until card (c), as the ruling binds.
- **Landing.** This seat flips the PR to ready and arms auto-merge through the relay now. At the merge, #25010 closes via `Fixes` and its `pm:dispatched` is removed. Card (c) of #24932 is then unblocked on the engine side.
